correctness.rationale: For fixed n the exact repulsive gamma=a Bloch edge factorization gives the band width as the difference of two confined harmonic-oscillator Dirichlet shifts. With u_n=H_n exp(-x²/2), the Wronskian derivative with respect to energy gives a growing-solution coefficient equal to minus the half-line L² mass. Reciprocal endpoint integration of 1/u_n² gives an explicit relative (n²+n+1)/(2a²) correction, while Dirichlet root Taylor remainders are exponentially smaller than the claimed O(a^-4) relative error. Subtracting the preceding shift changes the relative coefficient to (n+1)²/(2a²). The gamma function/Hermite norm fixes the prefactor. The actual standalone program passed 61 high-precision root, Robin-shift and coefficient checks; these are corroborating rather than exhaustive proofs.

originality.rationale: Scientific statement-level comparison: Gibbons–Veselov (2026) gives an exact gap length and Weber-function band edges and marks their precise low-band shrinkage as unresolved. Gannot (2014) proves existence of an all-orders confined-oscillator shift expansion and prints the leading coefficient with an unspecified O(a^-2) error, not its explicit next coefficient nor its modification by subtraction of adjacent shifts. Helffer–Kachmar–Nicoleau (2026) establish leading first-parameter Kummer zero asymptotics but not the displayed O(a^-2) coefficient. The other Kronig–Penney oscillator-well paper uses flat barriers rather than the point-interaction model. Targeted mathematical-record searches and accessible prior claims produced no identical evaluated two-term band-width statement. A previous paper or a further evaluation of generic confinement formulas could duplicate the coefficient; priority is not independent certification.
residual_risks: A not-yet-located older evaluation of a higher-order harmonic-oscillator confinement expansion could yield the same coefficient.

A general all-orders theorem of Gannot already proves existence of the asymptotic series, so novelty is restricted to the explicit band-width coefficient and its adjacent-edge contribution; literary priority remains best-knowledge only.

value.rationale: The motivating paper explicitly names precise exponentially shrinking low-index spectral bands as a natural open asymptotic regime. Their widths control the low-energy Bloch/tunneling scale. The displayed coefficient is the first nonleading correction for a canonical family with the unusual exact uniform gap length; it is not just the isolated-well correction, because the adjacent edge contributes at the same relative order. This improves relative accuracy from O(a^-2) to O(a^-4) for each fixed band and distinguishes neighboring excited bands. It is physically and mathematically motivated, and the statement does not assert a broader dispersion theorem.
